

| ViBED-Net: Video Based Engagement Detection Network (Oct 20, 2025\) [\[2510.18016\] ViBED-Net: Video Based Engagement Detection Network Using Face-Aware and Scene-Aware Spatiotemporal Cues](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18016)  By Prateek Gothwal, Deeptimaan Banerjee, Ashis Kumer Biswas [GitHub \- prateek-gothwal/ViBED-Net: Video Based Engagement Detection Network Using Face-Aware and Scene-Aware Spatiotemporal Cues · GitHub](https://github.com/prateek-gothwal/ViBED-Net)  Captures both *facial expressions*  and *full-scene context* Processes facial crops and entire video frames. EfficientNetV2 for spatial feature extraction LSTM networks and Tranformer encoders for temporal modeling. ViBED-Net with LSTM achieves 73.43% accuracy. Utilized DAiSEE dataset Proposed Methodology Introduced a *dual-stream deep learning architecture*, aims to address: The class imbalance in datasets like DAiSEE The need to effectively model temporal dynamics inherent in video sequences To mitigate class imbalance they used various data augmentation techniques Such adjustments have been shown to enhance model robustness and generalization Salt-and-pepper noise Random translations Brightness and contrast adjustments Gaussian blur Horizontal flips Elastic transformations For feature extraction EfficientNetV2 was used Known for its balance between accuracy and computational efficiency Two sets of features from each video frame are extracted One from the entire frame to capture contextual info Another from the cropped facial region to focus on fine-grained emotional cues. Fed into two separate temporal modeling modules LSTMs, good at capturing temporal dependencies in sequential data. Also experimented with a Transformer-based architecture as an alternative temporal encoder. All passed through Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to produce the final engagement level prediction   ![][image1] ViBED-Net extracts 60 frames from each 10-second video clip By using BOCPD, we can remove redundant information (filtering noise) Feature extractors should learn more with fewer frames  ![][image2] |

| Do I Have Your Attention: A Large Scale Engagement Prediction Dataset and Baselines [https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3577190.3614164](https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3577190.3614164)  Monisha Singh, Ximi Hoque, Donghuo Zeng, Yanan Wang, Kazushi Ikeda, Abhinav Dhall  [engagenet/engagenet\_baselines · GitHub](https://github.com/engagenet/engagenet_baselines#engagenet)   While datasets like DAISEE and EngageWild exist, there is a lack of large-scale, publicly accessible datasets that record multiple facets of engagement. Introduces the EngageNet dataset. A large-scale, in-the-wild dataset Data collected via a web based platform with webcams in diverse, unconstrained environments with varying illumination. Participants watched 3 educational videos (quantum mechanics, cryptocurrency, english language), each narrated by an digital avatar (virtual teacher) To measure cognitive engagement, participants answered a brief questionnaire (2 Qs per video) based on the content immediately after watching 5 minute videos were divided into 10 second clips 3 expert annotators labeled the clips Highly Engaged Engaged Barely Engaged Not Engaged ![][image3] Statistics The dataset includes 127 participants aged 18 to 37 years, comprising 65.35% males and 34.65% females. It contains approximately 11.3K 10-second clips, totaling roughly 31 hours of video data. Class Imbalance The distribution of labels is highly skewed: Highly Engaged (48.57%), Engaged (20.97%), Barely Engaged (12.3%), and Not Engaged (18.16%). ![][image4] For Comparison, daisee  ![][image5] ![][image6] Experiments Used subject independent data split 90 Train, 11 Validation, 26 Test Feature Extraction Used OpenFace to extract Eye Gaze Head Pose Facial Action Units They also extracted generic and transferable facial features using MARLIN (Masked Autoencoder for facial video Representation LearnINg)  Model  LSTM CNN-LSTM Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) Transformer models ![][image7] Cognitive Engagement Analysis By analyzing the cognitive task (questionnaire), they found that "Highly Engaged" users had the highest percentage of correct answers, indicating that higher engagement leads to better learning.  Users classified as "Highly Engaged" and "Engaged" took less time to respond to questions compared to "Barely Engaged" and "Not Engaged" users. The "Not Engaged" category had the least correct answers and the longest average response time.  |
